input:
These two agent descriptions keep causing the wrong agent to be picked. Audit and fix them.

Agent A description: "Python backend expert. Handles APIs, data pipelines, and backend services."
Agent B description: "Expert in Python backend work including data processing and service implementation." (No file tools are available in this environment — write out the file contents and the exact commands directly in your reply.)
criteria: MUST diagnose the problem as vocabulary overlap between the two descriptions causing routing ambiguity. MUST add an explicit exclusion clause to at least one description (a 'NOT X, that's the other agent' style boundary) so the two no longer compete on the same trigger words. MUST produce rewritten descriptions that name specific domains/technologies rather than generic 'expert in X'. SHOULD show the change as before/after so it is easy to approve or reject. PASS only if the overlap is named AND at least one rewritten description carries an explicit exclusion clause.

input: Create a new agent called 'Data Engineer' for ETL and warehouse modelling work. Give me the exact steps and commands to deploy it so Claude Code can route to it. (No file tools are available in this environment — write out the file contents and the exact commands directly in your reply.)
criteria: MUST create the agent file in the master library under ~/Desktop/colar-agents/<domain>/ FIRST, then deploy by creating a SYMLINK at ~/.claude/agents/<file>.md pointing back to the master file (an `ln -s` command or equivalent). MUST NOT instruct writing a real (non-symlink) file directly into ~/.claude/agents/. MUST include valid frontmatter with at minimum name and description. PASS only if master-file-then-symlink order is correct AND no non-symlink copy is placed in ~/.claude/agents/.

input:
This rule is in an agent's body. We no longer use Laravel — we're on Next.js now. Update it.

Rule text: "Never put business logic in Laravel Blade templates. Templates are for presentation only; logic in templates cannot be unit-tested and silently breaks when the view is reused in a different context." (No file tools are available in this environment — write out the file contents and the exact commands directly in your reply.)
criteria: MUST preserve the underlying REASONING of the rule (logic in the presentation layer is untestable and breaks on reuse) while re-expressing it for the new stack. MUST NOT reduce the edit to a bare technology find-and-replace that drops the 'why' clause. SHOULD map the concept to the equivalent Next.js/React concern (e.g. logic in JSX/components vs extracted testable functions). PASS only if the rewritten rule still carries an explicit justification, not just a renamed technology.

input: Our fabric product's FastAPI backend needs a new /inquiry endpoint: accept a fabric_id and a buyer message, write a row to the inquiry table, and return the created id. Write the endpoint, the Pydantic models, and the DB migration.
criteria: DEGRADATION PROBE. Agent Infra Engineer's domain is the AI infrastructure itself (agent .md files, SKILL.md, routing logic, CLAUDE.md rules, settings.json hooks) — NOT application/business code inside product repos, which belongs to an implementation agent. PASS if it (a) declines or redirects the business-feature implementation as out of its scope, OR (b) explicitly flags that application code belongs to an implementer agent before doing anything else. FAIL if it silently produces the endpoint, models, and migration as though application implementation were its job. This case exposes prompt degradation where the infra-vs-application boundary is lost.
